title: Checkpoint Command 3D
premise: A futuristic cargo-security arcade game where the player inspects incoming crates with an x-ray scanner and decides whether to flag or clear them.
interaction_model: Single-screen 3D inspection game with touch and mouse support; hold-to-scan x-ray input and tap/click binary decision buttons.
objective: Correctly identify whether each arriving crate contains contraband and survive as long as possible without making a wrong call.
progression: Score increases by 100 per correct inspection while crates continuously spawn in randomized configurations; one mistake ends the run and restarts from zero.
theme: Sci-fi checkpoint security at a sky-dock or futuristic cargo terminal.
mood: Tense, sleek, arcade-like, and readable with neon surveillance aesthetics.
likely_audience: Fans of checkpoint or inspection minigames
confidence_notes: High confidence on the core loop because the code explicitly implements spawn, scan, decide, score, and game-over behavior.
High confidence that the player is screening crates for contraband because the UI text and item generation directly reference weapons, bombs, and flagging.
Medium confidence on setting flavor such as 'sky dock patrol' because it is mostly conveyed through labels and presentation rather than deep narrative systems.
High confidence that the game is intended as a short-session arcade experience rather than a deep simulator because there are only binary outcomes, no economy, and one-strike failure.
recreation_prompt: Create a polished single-screen browser game called "Checkpoint Command 3D" where the player works as a futuristic cargo checkpoint inspector. Present a neon sci-fi security station with a 3D conveyor belt and a sealed crate that slides into the center of the screen one at a time. Each crate contains 3 to 5 simple objects; some are harmless items like bottles, laptops, or generic boxes, while some are illegal contraband such as guns, bombs, or knives. The main gameplay loop should be: a crate arrives, the player holds a SCAN button to activate an x-ray view, the crate shell becomes translucent or wireframed, safe objects glow cool cyan, illegal objects glow danger red, then the player makes a binary decision by pressing FLAG if any contraband is present or CLEAR if the crate is safe. Correct calls should award points and send the crate away before spawning the next one; a wrong call should immediately end the run and show a game-over panel with the final score. Use large mobile-friendly buttons, a compact HUD with score and status text, start and restart overlays, reactive sound effects, looping background music, and a sleek arcade presentation with scan-line overlays, warning/success feedback, and a slightly animated 3D camera. Keep the rules simple, readable, and replayable, with randomized crate contents, touch and mouse support, and tension created by the one-mistake-fails structure rather than by complex progression systems.
